info.title: CourtMesh Public API
info.summary: Programmatic access to Indian court judgments, orders and AI case analysis.
info.description:
The CourtMesh public API exposes the same case corpus that powers courtmesh.ai:
Supreme Court of India, all High Courts, District Courts and tribunals.

## Two search engines

The API offers two distinct search endpoints and they cover different corpora:

- `POST /search/cases` runs keyword and boolean search over the full OpenSearch index of 310M+ records.
  It is fast, exact and does not consume AI credits. Use it for case numbers, party names, citations,
  judge names and exact phrases.
- `POST /search/cases/semantic` runs vector similarity search over the roughly 2M case subset that has
  embeddings. It consumes AI credits and is slower. Use it for natural language questions about legal
  concepts, fact patterns and doctrines.

## Response envelope

Every endpoint except `GET /health` wraps its payload in a standard envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": ..., "meta": { ... }, "pagination": { ... } }
```

Failures inside a handler return `{ "success": false, "error": "..." }`. Failures raised by the
authentication middleware, which runs before the handler, return a bare `{ "error": "..." }` with no
`success` field. Clients should treat both as errors.

## Credits

Endpoints marked with the `ai` tag deduct AI credits from the account that owns the API key.
Keyword search, case retrieval, related documents, PDF links, judge search and timeline endpoints do not.

Most endpoints are 1 credit. The ones that are not:

| Endpoint | Credits |
|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{id}/pdf` | 5 |
| `POST /search/cases/semantic` | 10 |
| `POST /request-timeline` | 20 (1 when served from today's cached orders) |
| `POST /cases/{id}/analyze` | 100 (1 when an existing analysis is returned without re-running) |
| `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` | 400 |
| `POST /party/screen`, matches found | 100 |
| `POST /party/screen`, no matches found | 20 |
| `POST /party/screen` with `adjudicate: true` | add 80, so up to 180 for one call |

A 402 response (`code: "INSUFFICIENT_API_CREDITS"`) carries `required`, `balance`, `shortfall` and a
`topUpUrl`. Nothing is ever charged partway: a call either completes and is billed at the price above,
or it fails and nothing is deducted.

### Free tier AI lockout

The Free tier cannot call `POST /cases/{id}/analyze`, `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` or
`GET /cases/{id}/analysis` at all. Every one of the three refuses with `403` before any work happens
and before any credit is charged:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "code": "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED",
  "message": "AI analysis is not available on the Free tier. Upgrade to generate or read case analyses.",
  "tier": "free",
  "upgradeUrl": "https://research.courtmesh.ai/api/settings/api-keys#credits"
}
```

The Free tier keeps keyword search, case detail, related documents, judge search, PDF links, semantic
search and `POST /party/screen` (10 screens per month, deterministic only, see
"Litigation Check" below). There is no free monthly analyze allowance any more; upgrade to PAYG, Scale
or Enterprise for AI analysis.

## What a record is

A "record" is any case CourtMesh has indexed from a court registry: parties, dates, disposal status and
the docket. Not every record carries the underlying order or judgment text:

- **Document bearing** records have the order or judgment text indexed. `POST /search/cases`,
  `POST /search/cases/semantic`, `GET /cases/{id}`, `GET /cases/{id}/pdf`, `POST /cases/{id}/analyze` and
  `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` all work on document bearing records; the analyze endpoints
  fail with `400` on a record that has neither extracted text nor a stored PDF.
- **Status only** records are registry metadata with no document text yet: parties, case number, dates
  and disposal status, nothing to analyze or download. They are fully returned by
  `POST /search/cases`, `GET /cases/{id}` and `POST /party/screen`, but `hasDocuments` is `false` and
  `GET /cases/{id}/pdf` returns `404`.
- `total = documentBearing + statusOnly`. `GET /coverage` reports the split for the whole corpus and per
  court; a single case record does not carry a `recordType` field of its own, `hasDocuments` is the
  signal to read.

## Restricted records

A party can ask CourtMesh to withhold a case from search and screening under the case removal policy
(https://courtmesh.ai/case-removal-policy). This is a takedown, never a deletion: the record stays in
storage, and only its visibility through the public and API surfaces changes.

- A restricted case never appears in `POST /search/cases`, `POST /search/cases/semantic` or
  `POST /party/screen` results or in `relatedButUnverified`.
- A restricted case reached by its public case page returns `410 Gone`.
- A restricted case reached directly by `GET /cases/{id}`, `GET /cases/{id}/analysis`,
  `GET /cases/{id}/related` or `GET /cases/{id}/pdf` with its own id or case number is masked: the title
  and party names are replaced with a registry placeholder rather than the call failing outright.
- `POST /party/screen` discloses only a boolean, `coverage.someRecordsWithheld`, when a restricted case
  or a masked title was dropped from that screen. The count, the id and which candidate it was are never
  disclosed. A screen never reports `no_matches_found` on the strength of what withholding removed; see
  "Litigation Check" below for the exhaustiveness rule this follows.

## Rate limits

Every account has a per tier request budget enforced by `universalRateLimiter`, plus, on search
endpoints, a per tier ceiling on how much of the corpus one call or one page walk can touch:

| Tier | Requests/minute | Requests/day | Requests/month | Max page size (`limit`) | Max pagination depth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| free | 10 | 500 | 10,000 | 20 | 1,000 |
| payg | 60 | 20,000 | 4,00,000 | 50 | 10,000 |
| scale | 120 | 1,00,000 | 20,00,000 | 100 | 50,000 |
| enterprise | 600 | 10,00,000 | 2,00,00,000 | 100 | 1,00,000 |

The per minute ceiling produces `429` with `code: "RATE_LIMITED"` and a `Retry-After` header (see the
"RateLimited" response below). The page size and pagination depth ceilings apply only to
`POST /search/cases` and `POST /search/cases/semantic`, run after request validation, and produce `400`
rather than `429` because they reject the shape of the request rather than its frequency:

- `limit` above the tier's max page size: `400` `{ "success": false, "code": "PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "limit": ..., "tier": ... }`.
- `page * limit` above the tier's max pagination depth: `400` `{ "success": false, "code": "PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED", "limit": ..., "tier": ... }`.

`POST /party/screen` additionally carries its own, tighter per minute ceiling on top of the tier budget
above, plus a per tier cap on distinct names screened per day (repeat screens of a name already seen
today do not count against it, only genuinely new names do) and, on the Free tier only, a monthly screen
count cap:

| Tier | party/screen requests/minute | party/screen screens/month | Distinct names/day |
|---|---|---|---|
| free | 2 | 10 | 25 |
| payg | 10 | unlimited | 500 |
| scale | 30 | unlimited | 5000 |
| enterprise | 60 | unlimited | unlimited |

Hitting the per endpoint minute ceiling or the distinct names ceiling both produce `429` with a
`Retry-After` header, `code: "RATE_LIMITED"` for the former and `code: "DISTINCT_NAMES_LIMIT_REACHED"`
for the latter. Hitting the Free tier monthly screen count produces `403`
`code: "PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED"`, not `429`, because it resets monthly rather than
on a rolling window.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Find cases by keyword, by natural language meaning, or find judges by name.

tags.name: cases
tags.description: Retrieve a single case, its stored AI analysis, its sibling documents and its PDF link.

tags.name: ai
tags.description: Endpoints that run large language models on demand. These deduct AI credits from the account that owns the API key.

tags.name: timeline
tags.description: Fetch the live order and hearing history for a case from the court source systems. Asynchronous, request then poll.

tags.name: Litigation Check
tags.description: Screen a person or company name against the case corpus and get back confidence scored matches. See the endpoint description for the confidence model, the DPDP purpose requirement, and what restricted records mean here.

tags.name: Coverage
tags.description: Unauthenticated corpus coverage and freshness statistics: what CourtMesh has indexed, broken down by court, court type and year.

get.description:
Case insensitive substring search over the combined Supreme Court and High Court judge name lists.

Use this to resolve the exact spelling of a judge name before passing it as the `judgeName` filter to
`POST /search/cases`. Results are always capped at 50 names. Omitting `q`, or passing an empty `q`,
returns the first 50 names of the combined list rather than an error.

Does not consume AI credits.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring to match against judge names, case insensitive. Omit or leave empty to get the first 50 names.

query.description: The lower cased, trimmed search term that was applied.

totalMatches.description: Number of names returned, which is the capped count and not the total corpus match count.

500.description: Internal error. Returns `Judge data files are missing` when the server side judge lists cannot be read, otherwise `Internal server error`.

post.summary: Keyword search across all Indian court cases
post.description:
Keyword and boolean search over the full OpenSearch index of 310M+ Indian court records.
Fast, exact and free of AI credit cost.

Prefer this endpoint over `POST /search/cases/semantic` for case numbers, citations, party names,
judge names and exact phrases. Use the semantic endpoint for conceptual questions.

### Pagination

For the first few pages use `page`. For deep pagination pass the previous response's
`pagination.nextCursor` array back as `searchAfter` (JSON encode the array into the string), which
avoids the deep paging cost of large `page` values.

### Sorting

`sortBy` accepts `relevance` (default), `recent` (newest decision date first) and `oldest`.
`date` is a deprecated alias for `recent`: it is still accepted, and the response carries a
`meta.warnings` entry telling you what it was applied as. `meta.sortBy` always reports the sort that
was actually used.

### Filter notes

- `caseNumber` filters on the exact case number. The search service takes a single value, so an array
  with more than one entry is rejected with 400 rather than silently truncated.
- `judgeName`, `judges` and `judge` are three aliases for the same filter. The handler uses the first
  of them that is set, in that order.
- `meta.filters` reports the filters as they were applied.

data.description: Matching case documents. These are forwarded verbatim from the OpenSearch microservice and are NOT run through the response sanitizer, so the exact field set varies by court and by ingestion source. The properties listed here are the ones present on essentially every record; treat the object as open.

query.description: The free text portion of the query after inline filter parsing, which may differ from what you sent.

filters.description: Echo of the filters received, including ones that were not applied.

408.description: The upstream search query exceeded the 90 second budget.

example.error: Request timeout - OpenSearch query took too long

500.description: Internal error. Returns `OpenSearch API not configured` when the search backend is not wired up, otherwise `Internal server error`.

502.description: The search backend could not be reached.

post.summary: AI semantic search over embedded cases
post.description:
Vector similarity search over the case subset that has embeddings, roughly 2M records, which is a
much smaller corpus than the keyword index. Consumes AI credits and can take a minute or more.

Before searching, the service uses a language model to pull structured filters out of the natural
language query and to rewrite the remainder into legal terminology. The top level filter parameters
override what the model extracted, and the nested `filters` object overrides both.

### Important behaviours you must code for

- **The status code reflects the outcome.** An earlier version of this handler flushed a 200 before
  doing any work, so failures arrived as HTTP 200 with a `{"success": false}` body. They no longer do:
  an embedding or vector search failure is a 502, and an unexpected failure is a 500. A search that
  ran and matched nothing is still a 200 with an empty `data` array.
- **Filters are applied where you put them.** Every top level filter parameter is mapped onto a vector
  store key and reported in `meta.appliedFilters`. Two of them are narrower than on the keyword
  endpoint because of what the vector index can express: `caseNumber` must be digits only, and only
  one judge name can be filtered per request. Both are rejected with 400 rather than dropped.
- **Filter only queries fall back to keyword search.** If the model strips the query down to fewer
  than 3 characters, the request is served by the keyword engine instead and `meta.fallbackMode` is
  set to `opensearch`.
- **`pagination.total` is an estimate.** The handler fetches one extra row to detect whether another
  page exists, so `total` and `totalPages` are exact only on the final page.

value.query: when can a court lift the corporate veil to hold directors personally liable for company debts
medical negligence standard of care for surgeons

200.description: Semantic search results. Returned only when the search actually ran, including when it matched nothing, in which case `data` is empty and `meta.message` explains it.

originalQuery.description: Present only when normalisation changed the query.

appliedFilters.description: The filters actually applied to the search: model extracted filters, overridden by the top level parameters, overridden by the nested `filters` object, after court and case type expansion.

fallbackMode.description: Present only when the query was filter only and the request was served by the keyword engine.

message.description: Present when there were no hits, for example `No similar cases found.`

403.description: AI credits are exhausted or the plan does not permit AI interactions.

408.description: The request exceeded the 10 minute handler timeout.

502.description: An upstream dependency failed: the embedding provider, the vector store, or the keyword engine behind the filter only fallback.

get.description:
Returns the metadata for a single case, deliberately WITHOUT the AI analysis. Call
`GET /cases/{id}/analysis` for the analysis.

`detailedSummary`, `headnote`, `holding` and `keyFacts` are not part of this payload by design; they
live on the analysis endpoint.

Does not consume AI credits.

note.example: Use /cases/:id/analysis endpoint to get AI analysis separately

get.summary: Get the stored AI analysis for a case
get.description:
Returns the AI analysis already stored against a case. This endpoint is read only: it never triggers
analysis and never consumes AI credits.

When no analysis exists the call still succeeds with `hasAnalysis: false`, a `message` field and no
`analysis` key. Generate one with `POST /cases/{id}/analyze` and poll this endpoint after roughly 30
to 60 seconds.

Fields that are absent on the stored analysis are stripped rather than
returned as null, so treat every property inside `analysis` as optional.

200.description: Analysis payload, or a `hasAnalysis: false` marker.

note.description: Empty string when analysis exists, otherwise `Use POST /cases/:id/analyze to generate AI analysis`.

data.message: AI analysis not available for this case

meta.note: Use POST /cases/:id/analyze to generate AI analysis

get.summary: Get sibling documents and the procedural timeline for a case
get.description:
Returns every stored document that shares the same case number as the given case, plus a timeline
derived from those documents.

This is NOT similarity search. It answers "what else exists in this same matter", not "what other
cases are like this one". For similar cases use `POST /search/cases/semantic`.

Behaviour worth knowing:

- Related documents are capped at 50 and returned newest first.
- Only documents that have both a decision date and a stored PDF appear in `timeline`.
- `timeline` entries are sorted oldest first, and the earliest entry is relabelled `Case Initiated`
  unless it is already a `Final Judgment`.
- If the case has no case number the call still succeeds with two empty arrays and
  `meta.message: "No case number found for this case"`.

Does not consume AI credits.

message.description: Only present when the case has no case number.

get.summary: Get a time limited link to the case PDF
get.description:
Returns a link to the official judgment or order PDF held in CourtMesh storage.

**The returned `pdfUrl` is an encrypted presigned URL, not a directly fetchable link.** It is a
presigned S3 URL that has then been encrypted with a case specific key, and it must be decrypted
client side before it can be opened. The underlying presigned URL expires after 3600 seconds.

Returns 404 with `PDF not available for this case` when the case has no stored document.

Does not consume AI credits.

note.example: The PDF URL is encrypted and expires in 1 hour. Use the decryption key provided in your SDK.

404.description: Either the case does not exist (`Case not found`) or it has no stored document (`PDF not available for this case`).

post.summary: Trigger AI analysis of a single case
post.description:
Starts AI analysis of one case. **Consumes AI credits.**

This is asynchronous. The normal response is `202 Accepted` with `status: "processing"`, and the work
continues in the background. Poll `GET /cases/{id}/analysis` after roughly 30 to 60 seconds.

If the case already has an analysis and `force` is false, the endpoint short circuits with `200` and
returns the existing analysis inline, with `alreadyExists: true`. Pass `force: true` to re analyse.

The background job prefers file based analysis of the stored PDFs and falls back to analysing the
extracted text. If neither the extracted text nor a PDF source is available the request is rejected
with `400` before any credit is spent. Note that credit exhaustion is detected inside the background
job, so it surfaces in server logs rather than in this response.

**Consumes 100 credits (1 when `alreadyExists: true` is returned).**
On the Free tier this endpoint refuses with `403` `code: "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED"` before any work or
charge; see "Credits" above.

200.description: An analysis already existed and `force` was not set, so it is returned as is.

202.description: Analysis accepted and started in the background.

note.example: You can check the analysis status by calling the GET /cases/:id endpoint in 30-60 seconds.

400.description: Either request validation failed, or the case has no analysable content: `Case does not have sufficient content for analysis. Case must have at least 100 characters of text or documents with s3Key to generate AI analysis.`

post.summary: AI analysis across every document in a matter
post.description:
Runs one AI analysis over all the documents that share the case number, producing a single merged
view of the whole matter rather than of one judgment. **Consumes substantially more AI credits than
`POST /cases/{id}/analyze`.**

Unlike the single case endpoint this one is **synchronous**: it blocks until the model finishes, which
can take minutes. Set a long client timeout.

Document selection depends on the court:

- High Court: the case document plus up to the 5 most recent orders attached to it.
- Supreme Court: up to 20 documents sharing the case number.

The combined text is truncated to 100,000 characters before analysis. The result is cached against
the case number, so a second call returns `status: "already_analyzed"` unless `force` is true.

**Consumes 400 credits.** On the Free tier this endpoint refuses with
`403` `code: "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED"` before any work or charge; see "Credits" above.

200.description: Consolidated analysis, freshly generated or served from cache.

relatedCases.description: Number of case documents that fed the analysis. Absent on the cached path.

400.description: Validation failed, or the case has no case number (`Case number is required for consolidated analysis`), or none of the documents carry text (`No text content available for analysis`).

404.description: `Case not found`, or `No related cases or orders found`.

500.description: `Consolidated AI analysis failed` when the model returns nothing, otherwise `Internal server error`.

post.summary: Screen a person or company name against the case corpus
post.description:
Searches the corpus for cases naming the given person or company, resolves how likely each
candidate is to actually be that party, and returns confidence scored matches. Tagged `ai` because
the optional `adjudicate: true` pass runs a language model over the uncertain middle; the
deterministic core (name similarity, identifier matching) always runs and never calls a model.

### Pricing

A screen that finds at least one match costs 100 credits. A screen that finds
none costs only 20: the retrieval work is the same either way, but a
genuine negative did not produce anything to analyse. `adjudicate: true` adds a flat
80 credit surcharge whenever it is requested, regardless of how
many candidates actually needed the model (at most 40 per call), so the
most one call can ever cost is 180 credits. `meta.creditsCharged`
reports what this call actually cost; reconstruct your bill from it rather than assuming the price
table, since the no-match price applies whenever `summary.matchCount` is 0 regardless of what you
expected going in.

### Confidence bands

Each match carries `confidence.band`, one of four values, driven by a calibrated match probability
`confidence.score` between 0 and 1:

| Band | Score | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `confirmed` | >= 0.90, or an exact statutory identifier match (PAN, GSTIN, CIN, LLPIN) | High confidence this candidate is the searched party. |
| `probable` | >= 0.70 | Strong name and context evidence, short of confirmed. |
| `possible` | >= 0.45 | Plausible but weak evidence; review before acting on it. |
| `unlikely` | below 0.45, or an identifier conflict | Shown only if it clears `displayThreshold`; usually filtered out. |

**A person is never auto-confirmed on name evidence alone.** For `entityType: "person"`, a name-only
match is capped below the `confirmed` threshold even at a perfect name similarity; the candidate can
only reach `confirmed` through an exact identifier match, or, with `adjudicate: true`, a model that
still respects the same cap on a common name with no disambiguator. This mirrors the identical rule
in CourtMesh's CLM counterparty screening, on purpose: the same name, however common, must never be
silently treated as one person across products.

`confidence.engine` is `"rules"` when the deterministic core produced the band, or `"llm"` when
`adjudicate: true` was set and the model actually reviewed that candidate (it does not run on every
candidate: only the ones the deterministic core could not already decide, capped at
40 per call, cheapest and most ambiguous first).

### The verdict and exhaustiveness

`summary.verdict` is `"matches_found"` whenever `matches` is non-empty. It is `"no_matches_found"`
ONLY when the underlying search was actually exhaustive for this name
(`coverage.exhaustive || coverage.exhaustiveWithinFilters`). Anything short of that, a plan clamp, a
strategy that errored, a merely partial run, reports `"inconclusive"` instead: an absence of matches
is never reported as an absence of litigation history unless the retrieval genuinely covered the
corpus. Read `coverage.strategiesRun`, `coverage.planClamped` and `coverage.anyStrategyErrored` to
see why a call came back inconclusive.

### Restricted records

A case withheld under the case removal policy, or one still carrying a registry masking token on its
title, is dropped before scoring and never appears in `matches` or `relatedButUnverified`.
`coverage.someRecordsWithheld` is the ONLY signal this happened: it is a plain boolean, never a count
or an id, and it does not by itself flip the verdict away from `"matches_found"` when other matches
still stand. See "Restricted records" above for the full policy.

### DPDP and logging

`purpose` is required so the caller states, per DPDP section 5 grounds, why this name is being
processed before CourtMesh does any work on it. The searched `name`, `aliases`, `knownPersons`,
`identifiers` and `address` are never written to any log or to `api_key_transactions`: only their
lengths and counts are, alongside `purpose`, `entityType`, the match count and whether adjudication
ran. This is the same data minimisation `POST /search/cases/semantic` and the internal screening
service already follow.

### relatedButUnverified

Candidates the search layer surfaced but that did not clear the scoring floor, or exist only to show
why a stronger match was preferred, are returned separately in `relatedButUnverified` with only the
plain case fields, no `confidence`, `evidence`, `partyRole` or `rationale`. Treat these as leads to
review manually, not as scored results.

personWithAliases.summary: Screen a person, with aliases and an address disambiguator

200.description: Screen completed. Present even when `summary.matchCount` is 0.

creditsCharged.description: What this call actually cost: the match or no-match base price, plus the adjudication surcharge if `adjudicate` was true. See "Pricing" above.

corpusAsOf.description: The `generatedAt` timestamp of the coverage snapshot in effect when this screen ran (the same value `GET /coverage` reports). A rough freshness bound on the corpus this screen searched, not a per case timestamp.

403.description:
One of three refusals, distinguished by `code`, all produced before any work or charge:

- `API_NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_TRIAL`: the account is still on trial. API access, including
  this endpoint, is not available during trial.
- `API_ENTERPRISE_ONLY`: self serve tiers are off and this key is not Enterprise.
- `PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED`: the Free tier's
  `10` screens per month cap is reached. Only the Free tier has
  a monthly screen cap; every other tier is unlimited here (the per minute and distinct-names
  ceilings in "Rate limits" above still apply to all tiers).

value.error: API access is not available during trial. It unlocks automatically when your trial ends or you upgrade.

monthlyCapReached.summary: Free tier monthly screen cap reached

429.description:
Two different limiters can produce this status, distinguished by `code`:

- `code: "RATE_LIMITED"`: this endpoint's own, tighter per minute ceiling (see the
  `party/screen requests/minute` column in "Rate limits" above) was exceeded, on top of the
  account's overall per minute budget.
- `code: "DISTINCT_NAMES_LIMIT_REACHED"`: the tier's distinct-names-per-day cap was exceeded.
  Repeat screens of a name already seen today do not count against this; only new names do.

Both set a `Retry-After` header in seconds and share the `RateLimitError` body shape.

value.message: Too many requests. This endpoint allows 10 requests per minute.
This tier allows 25 distinct names per day.

post.summary: Request the live order and hearing history for a case
post.description:
Starts a job that fetches the current order and hearing history for a case from the court source
systems. Poll the returned `requestId` with `GET /get-timeline/{requestId}`.

`case_id` must be the 24 character MongoDB ObjectId of the case, which is the `id` field returned by
the search and case endpoints. A case number will not work here.

Behaviour differs by court:

- Supreme Court cases return immediately with `status: "completed"`, `orderCount: 0` and a message
  explaining that SC cases have no separate orders.
- District Court cases are fetched synchronously and come back `completed` or `failed`.
- High Court cases are queued and normally come back `pending`, so they need polling. If orders were
  already fetched today the response is served from cache with `cached: true` and the orders inline.

This endpoint has no zod schema. `case_id` is checked manually: it must be present and must be a 24
character hexadecimal id, otherwise the request is rejected with 400.
Does not consume AI credits.

200.description: Job accepted, or cached orders returned inline.

400.description: `case_id is required`, or `case_id must be a 24 character hexadecimal case id` when the value cannot be an ObjectId.

get.description:
Returns the status, and when finished the payload, of a job created by `POST /request-timeline`.

Poll until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. When orders have been fetched they arrive in `orders`,
with `orderCount` for this response and `totalOrderCount` for the case overall. The generic `result`
object is only included when `totalOrderCount` is absent, to avoid two competing representations of
the same data.

Does not consume AI credits.

200.description: Job status and, when available, the fetched orders.

get.description:
**No API key required.** This is the "check our numbers before you buy" surface: it is meant to be
callable straight from curl or from the public coverage page, so it sits outside the metered key
authentication every other endpoint on this page requires and outside the credit system entirely.

Backed by a 6 hour server side cache (`coverage:v1`) of a query against the OpenSearch index, with a
stale-serve fallback: an expired cache still serves its last known snapshot while a refresh is
attempted in the background, rather than blocking the request or failing it. Only a cold cache with
the source unreachable returns `503`.

`data.total = data.documentBearing + data.statusOnly`. See "What a record is" above for what those
two counts mean. `data.districtCourts` is one rolled up row rather than a row per court: the index
carries no state field to group District Courts by today.

`Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600` is set on a `200`;
`Cache-Control: no-store` on a `503`. CORS is permissive: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is set for
every caller (courtmesh.ai and any configured marketing origin get their own origin reflected back;
anyone else, including a bare curl with no `Origin` header, gets a usable wildcard-equivalent value
rather than being refused), because the data is identical and public for every caller regardless of
origin.

200.description: Coverage snapshot, fresh or served stale from cache.

generatedAt.description: Same value as `data.generatedAt`, repeated here so callers who only read `meta` still get it.

cacheTtlSeconds.description: How long a snapshot is served before a refresh is attempted. Currently 6 hours.

corpusNote.description: Plain language explanation of documentBearing vs statusOnly, repeated here so the field is self describing without reading this page.
corpusNote.example: A record is any case CourtMesh has indexed from a court registry (parties, dates, status, docket). "documentBearing" counts records that also have the order or judgment text indexed; the rest are "statusOnly", registry metadata with no document text yet. total = documentBearing + statusOnly.

503.description: The cache is cold (nothing to serve stale) and the coverage source could not be reached.

example.error: Coverage data is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.

get.description:
Unauthenticated liveness check. This is the only endpoint that requires no API key and the only one
that does not use the standard `data` envelope.

ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyHeader.description:
CourtMesh API key sent in the `X-API-Key` header.

Keys look like `cm-` followed by 32 base64url characters, a hyphen, then 4 more base64url characters.
Legacy keys issued with the `vv-` prefix are still accepted. Keys that do not match that shape are
rejected with `401 Invalid API key format` before any lookup happens.

BearerAuth.description: The same API key may instead be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The `X-API-Key` header takes precedence when both are present.

CaseId.name: id
CaseId.description:
Either the 24 character MongoDB ObjectId of the case, or its case number.

A 24 character hexadecimal value is looked up by `_id` first, and if no document matches it is then
looked up as a case number. Anything else goes straight to the case number lookup. 404 means neither
lookup found a document.

Unauthorized.description:
The API key is missing, malformed, unknown or deactivated. This is produced by the authentication
middleware before the handler runs, so the body is a bare `{ "error": "..." }` with no `success` field.

Observed messages: `API key required. Provide it in X-API-Key header or Authorization: Bearer <key>`,
`Invalid API key format`, `Invalid API key`, `API key is deactivated`.

Forbidden.description:
The key is valid but the account is not allowed to make this call. Produced by the authentication
middleware, so the body is a bare `{ "error": "..." }`.

Causes: `Organization is deactivated`, `Account is suspended`, `Billing is inactive for this account`,
`Account not found`, a caller IP that is not on the organisation IP whitelist, or the daily API call
quota being exhausted. The quota case adds `callsToday` and `maxAllowed` alongside `error`.

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests. Two different limiters can produce this status.

The plan level limiter returns `{ "error": "Rate limit exceeded" }`. The per minute limiter returns
the richer body shown here, including `retryAfter` in seconds and a `code` (`RATE_LIMITED` for a
plain per minute ceiling; `POST /party/screen` can also return `DISTINCT_NAMES_LIMIT_REACHED` here,
see that endpoint's own 429 documentation). Back off for `retryAfter` seconds when the field is
present.

example.message: Too many requests. Maximum 60 requests per minute allowed.

TierNotAllowed.description:
The Free tier cannot call this endpoint at all: `TIER_LIMITS.free.analysisReadAllowed` is `false`,
so `GET /cases/{id}/analysis` refuses every Free tier caller with this response before any work
happens. See "Credits" above for the full Free tier AI lockout.

example.message: AI analysis is not available on the Free tier. Upgrade to generate or read case analyses.

ForbiddenOrTierNotAllowed.description:
Either AI credits are exhausted or the account's plan does not permit AI interactions at all
(`ErrorEnvelope`, no `code`), or, when the caller is on the Free tier, this endpoint refuses outright
before any work or charge (`TierNotAllowedError`, `code: "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED"`, carries
`upgradeUrl`). See "Credits" above for the Free tier AI lockout.

aiCreditsExhausted.summary: AI credits exhausted or plan does not permit AI

value.message: AI analysis is not available on the Free tier. Upgrade to generate or read case analyses.

InsufficientApiCredits.description:
The account's API credit wallet does not cover this call's price. Nothing is charged. `required` is
the credits this call would have cost, `balance` is the wallet balance at the time of the check, and
`shortfall` is `required - balance`. `wallet` is always `"api_credits"`, naming which of the two
wallets this is (never the in app platform wallet, which API calls never touch), and `walletOwner`
is `"user"` or `"org"`. `topUpUrl` links to the credit purchase surface; on an org owned wallet a
non admin caller gets `contactAdmin: true` instead, since only an admin can top it up.

example.message: This call needs 100 credits and the wallet has 42.

StandingUnavailable.description: The identity service could not confirm the account standing, so the request was refused rather than allowed through. Retry with backoff. Body is a bare `{ "error": "Unable to verify account standing. Please retry." }`.

example.error: Unable to verify account standing. Please retry.

ValidationFailed.description: Request body failed zod validation. `details` lists one human readable message per offending field, in `field: message` form.

example.error: Validation failed. Please check your request and try again.
details: query: Search query cannot be empty. Please provide a search term.
limit: Limit cannot exceed 100 results per page.

ValidationFailedOrTierCapExceeded.description:
Either zod request validation failed (`ValidationErrorEnvelope`, has `error` and `details`), or,
after validation passed, the per tier query-shape guard rejected the request's `page`/`limit` shape
(`TierCapExceededError`, has `code` and `tier`, no `error` field). See "Rate limits" above for the
per tier `maxPageSize` and `maxPaginationDepth` values these two codes enforce:

- `code: "PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"`: `limit` is above this tier's max page size.
- `code: "PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED"`: `page * limit` is above this tier's max pagination depth.

value.error: Validation failed. Please check your request and try again.
details: query: Search query cannot be empty. Please provide a search term.
limit: Limit cannot exceed 100 results per page.

pageLimitExceeded.summary: limit above this tier's max page size

paginationDepthExceeded.summary: page * limit above this tier's max pagination depth

example.error: Invalid URL parameters. Please check your request and try again.
details: id: Case ID cannot be empty. Please provide a valid case ID or case number.

CaseNotFound.description: No case matches the supplied id or case number.

BareError.title: BareError
BareError.description: Error shape produced by middleware that runs before the route handler. It has no `success` field.

code.description: Machine readable refusal code. Not present on every 403 (the oldest causes, an inactive org or a bad IP, predate this field), but present on every refusal added since: `API_ENTERPRISE_ONLY`, `API_NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_TRIAL`, `API_KEY_LIMIT_REACHED`, `FREE_TIER_AI_CAP_REACHED`, `PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED`.

callsToday.description: Present only when the refusal is a daily API call quota, or a monthly cap reported the same way (for example `PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED`).

maxAllowed.description: Present only when the refusal is a daily API call quota, or a monthly cap reported the same way.

TierNotAllowedError.title: TierNotAllowedError
TierNotAllowedError.description: Refusal shape for API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED: the Free tier calling an endpoint it has no access to at all. Distinct from ForbiddenError: it always carries `success`, `code` and `upgradeUrl`.

message.example: AI analysis is not available on the Free tier. Upgrade to generate or read case analyses.

TierCapExceededError.title: TierCapExceededError
TierCapExceededError.description: Returned by the per tier query-shape guard (server/middleware/api-tier-limits.ts), which runs after zod validation on `POST /search/cases` and `POST /search/cases/semantic`. No `error` field on this shape; check `code` instead.

InsufficientApiCreditsError.title: InsufficientApiCreditsError
InsufficientApiCreditsError.description: HTTP 402. The API credit wallet does not cover this call. See the InsufficientApiCredits response for what each field means.

required.description: Credits this call would have cost.

balance.description: Wallet balance at the time of the check.

contactAdmin.description: Present instead of `topUpUrl` when the wallet is org owned and this caller is not an admin.

success.description: Present on the per minute and per endpoint limiters; absent on the older plan level limiter body.

code.description: Present on the per minute and per endpoint limiters.

message.description: Present on the per minute limiter only.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until the window resets. Present on the per minute limiter only.

resetTime.description: When the window resets. Present on the per minute limiter only.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope
ErrorEnvelope.description: Error shape produced inside a route handler.

details.description: One message per offending field. Absent on non validation 400s.

SearchPagination.title: SearchPagination
SearchPagination.description: Pagination block for keyword search. It is the pagination object returned by the search backend with `hasMore` recomputed by the API layer. Note that `totalPages` is only present on the degraded path where the backend returned no pagination at all, so do not depend on it; use `hasMore` and `nextCursor`.

totalPages.description: Only present on the degraded fallback path.

nextCursor.description: Sort values of the last hit. JSON encode this array and send it back as `searchAfter` to fetch the next page.

EstimatedPagination.title: EstimatedPagination
EstimatedPagination.description: Pagination block for semantic search. `total` and `totalPages` are conservative estimates derived from fetching one extra row, and are exact only on the final page.

query.description: Search terms. Trimmed, and must not be empty after trimming.

court.description: Court name or names, matched verbatim against the index spelling, for example `Bombay High Court`. Comma separated strings are also split.

year.description: Year of decision. Accepts an integer, a 4 digit string, or an array of either. Integers are bounded to 1947 (Indian independence) through the current year.

caseType.description: Case type code or primary type. Primary types such as `Appeal` are expanded server side into their component codes.

caseNumber.description: Exact case number filter, forwarded to the search service. Single valued: a string, or an array of at most one string. An array with more than one entry is rejected with 400.

judgeName.description: Judge name filter. Use `GET /judges/search` to resolve exact spellings.

judges.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` is absent.

judge.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` and `judges` are both absent.

fromDate.description: Inclusive lower bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

toDate.description: Inclusive upper bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

searchAfter.description: Deep pagination cursor. JSON encode the `pagination.nextCursor` array from the previous response, for example `"[12.483261,\"000000000000000000000000\"]"`. A single scalar value is also accepted.

sortBy.description: Sort order. `relevance` (default), `recent` (newest decision date first) or `oldest`. `date` is a deprecated alias for `recent`, kept so callers written against the old schema keep working; when you send it the response includes a `meta.warnings` entry. `meta.sortBy` reports the sort actually applied.

SemanticSearchRequest.title: SemanticSearchRequest
SemanticSearchRequest.description: The top level filter parameters use the same names as `POST /search/cases` and are mapped onto the vector store keys: `court` to `court`, `year` to `caseYear`, `caseType` to `caseType`, `caseNumber` to `caseNumber`, `judgeName`/`judges`/`judge` to `judgeName`, and `fromDate`/`toDate` to the `decisionDate` range. Precedence, weakest first: filters the model inferred from `query`, then these top level parameters, then the nested `filters` object. `meta.appliedFilters` reports the result.

query.description: Natural language description of what you are looking for. At least 3 characters.
query.example: when can a court lift the corporate veil to hold directors personally liable

court.description: Court name or names, matched against the vector store `court` payload key. A High Court representative name is expanded to its member spellings. Comma separated strings are also split.

year.description: Year of decision. Accepts an integer, a 4 digit string, or an array of either. Integers are bounded to 1947 (Indian independence) through the current year.

caseType.description: Case type code or primary type, mapped to the `caseType` payload key. Primary types such as `Appeal` are expanded server side into their component codes.

caseNumber.description: Case number, digits only, for example `1234`. The vector index stores case numbers as integers, so a value containing anything other than digits is rejected with 400. Use `POST /search/cases` to filter on a full case number string.

judgeName.description: Single judge name, matched against the indexed `judges` values, so it must be the exact indexed spelling. Use `GET /judges/search` to resolve it. A one element array is also accepted; more than one judge is rejected with 400 because the vector store matches one name at a time.

judges.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` is absent.

judge.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` and `judges` are both absent.

fromDate.description: Inclusive lower bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Applied as `decisionDate.$gte`.

toDate.description: Inclusive upper bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Applied as `decisionDate.$lte`.

limit.description: Results per page. The handler additionally clamps this to 100.

filters.description: Vector store filters addressed directly. These take precedence over the top level parameters and over anything the model extracted from `query`. Keys the downstream layer understands: `court`, `courtType`, `courtName`, `caseType`, `caseYear`, `registrationYear`, `decisionYear`, `judgeName`, `caseNumber`, `practiceArea`, `precedentValue`, and `decisionDate` with `$gte` and `$lte` sub keys.

force.description: Re run the analysis even when one already exists. Costs credits every time.

case_id.description: The 24 character MongoDB ObjectId of the case, as returned in the `id` field elsewhere in this API. A case number is not accepted, and a value that is not 24 hexadecimal characters is rejected with 400.

PartyScreenRequest.title: PartyScreenRequest
PartyScreenRequest.description: Mirrors partyScreenSchema (server/utils/api-v1-validations.ts) field for field. `additionalProperties` is not set to false here because the schema itself has no `.strict()` at the top level; `identifiers` and `address` are individually strict.

name.description: The person or company name to screen. Trimmed.

aliases.description: Alternate names to screen alongside `name`. At most 7: the name plus its aliases must fit within the 8 name screening limit.

entityType.description: Required. Drives the confidence model: a `person` can never be auto-confirmed on name evidence alone, see the endpoint description.

purpose.description: Required. Why this name is being screened, per DPDP section 5 grounds. Never logged alongside the name itself, only alongside counts.

identifiers.description: Statutory identifiers. Each is format and check digit validated (server/services/entity-resolution/name-utils.ts) and rejected with 400 if malformed, rather than silently passed through as an unmatchable string. An exact match on any of these is the only way a `person` screen can reach the `confirmed` confidence band.

address.description: A weak corroborating signal, not an identifier: narrows ambiguity on a common name but never alone reaches `confirmed`.

knownPersons.description: Names of directors, officers or known associates. Another corroborating signal, used the same way as `address`.

court.description: Restrict the screen to one or more courts. The internal search service accepts a single court filter, so only the first entry of an array is honoured; this is a documented limitation, not a validation error.

since.description: Only consider cases with a decision or filing date on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Best effort: a case with neither date is kept rather than dropped.

limit.description: Maximum candidates to retrieve before scoring.

adjudicate.description: Run the LLM adjudication pass over the uncertain middle (up to 40 candidates), adding the 80 credit surcharge. See "Pricing" on the endpoint.

displayThreshold.description: Minimum calibrated match probability for a candidate to appear in `matches`, default 0.6. A `confirmed` match is always shown regardless of this threshold.

OpenSearchCaseHit.title: OpenSearchCaseHit
OpenSearchCaseHit.description: A search hit forwarded verbatim from the OpenSearch microservice. The API layer does NOT run these through the response sanitizer, and the code types them as `unknown[]`, so the exact field set is not pinned down anywhere in the source. The properties listed below are the ones present on essentially every record across Supreme Court, High Court and District Court ingestion; additional court specific fields may be present. Treat this object as open.

id.description: Case identifier, usable as the `{id}` path parameter.

decisionDate.description: ISO date or date-time, depending on the source record.

CaseListItem.title: CaseListItem
CaseListItem.description: Compact case record returned by semantic search. Undefined fields are stripped, so treat everything except `id` as optional.

similarity.description: Vector similarity score, roughly 0 to 1. Added by the semantic search handler only, and the minimum score threshold is 0.3.

CaseDetails.title: CaseDetails
CaseDetails.description: Case metadata. Undefined fields are stripped, so treat everything except `id` as optional. `detailedSummary`, `headnote`, `holding` and `keyFacts` are deliberately excluded and live on the analysis endpoint.

metadata.description: Present only when the source record carries a diary number.

hasAnalysis.description: True when a stored AI analysis with a summary exists. Fetch it from `/cases/{id}/analysis`.

CaseAnalysisResult.title: CaseAnalysisResult
CaseAnalysisResult.description: When `hasAnalysis` is false the object carries `message` and no `analysis` key.

message.const: AI analysis not available for this case

AnalysisBody.title: AnalysisBody
AnalysisBody.description: The AI analysis. Every property is optional: fields the model did not produce are stripped before the response is sent.

issues.description: Legal issues paired with the court holding on each.

citedCases.description: Cited authorities bucketed by how this judgment treated them.

StoredAnalysis.title: StoredAnalysis
StoredAnalysis.description: The analysis object as stored, returned by the two analyze endpoints. It is passed through `sanitizeAnalysis`, which only strips the internal `analysisModel`, `analysisVersion`, `analysisDate` and `analysisMethod` fields, so it is a superset of `AnalysisBody`: it also carries `outcome`, `benchComposition`, `opinionType`, `factPattern` and `linkedCases`. Every property is optional.

relatedDocuments.description: Documents sharing this case number, newest first, capped at 50.

isCurrent.description: True for the document you asked about.

timeline.description: Chronological procedural events, oldest first. Only documents that have both a decision date and a stored PDF appear here, so this is usually shorter than `relatedDocuments`.

status.description: Derived from the document case type and disposal nature. The earliest entry is relabelled `Case Initiated` unless it is already a `Final Judgment`.

statusLabel.description: The disposal nature when present, otherwise the same value as `status`.

pdfUrl.description: An encrypted presigned S3 URL. It is NOT directly fetchable: decrypt it client side with the case specific key first.

expiresIn.description: Lifetime of the underlying presigned URL in seconds.

cached.description: Present when the response was served from orders already fetched today.

message.description: Human readable context, present on cached and short circuit paths.

orders.description: Order records, present only when orders were already available. The order document shape is assembled dynamically from the source court record and is not typed in the source, so treat each entry as an open object.

result.description: Generic job result. Included only when `totalOrderCount` is absent, so that there is one representation of the orders rather than two. Untyped in the source.

orders.description: Fetched orders. Untyped in the source, treat each entry as an open object.

totalOrderCount.description: Orders known for the case overall.

MatchSignal.title: MatchSignal
MatchSignal.description: One piece of evidence the confidence score was built from.

name.description: What this signal checks, for example `pan`, `name_similarity`, `address_city`.

evidence.description: The exact input token(s) this signal is grounded in. No information from outside the request or the candidate case.

PartyScreenCaseFields.title: PartyScreenCaseFields
PartyScreenCaseFields.description: Plain case fields shared by every entry in `matches` and `relatedButUnverified`. Undefined fields are stripped, so treat everything except `caseId` as optional.

caseId.description: Usable as the `{id}` path parameter on the case endpoints.

PartyScreenMatch.title: PartyScreenMatch
PartyScreenMatch.description: One scored candidate. See the endpoint description for what the confidence bands mean and the rule that a person is never auto-confirmed on name evidence alone.

partyRole.description: The searched party's apparent role in this case.

score.description: Alias of `calibrated`, kept as a stable top level "the number" field.

engine.description: `llm` only when `adjudicate: true` was requested and the model actually reviewed this candidate.

strategies.description: Which retrieval strategies surfaced this candidate.

nameSimilarity.description: Best name similarity between the searched name (or an alias) and this candidate.

disambiguatorPresent.description: Whether an identifier, address or known-person disambiguator was available for this candidate, not just a bare name.

rationale.description: Present when the deterministic core or the LLM produced an explanation.

exhaustive.description: The retrieval covered the full corpus for this name.

exhaustiveWithinFilters.description: The retrieval covered the full corpus within the filters given (`court`, `since`), even if not the whole corpus.

planClamped.description: The account's plan limited how much retrieval this call could do.

anyStrategyErrored.description: At least one retrieval strategy failed; the run is not exhaustive even if others succeeded.

someRecordsWithheld.description: A case was dropped because it is restricted under the case removal policy, or its title carried a masking token. This is the ONLY disclosure made about withheld records: never a count, an id, or which candidate it was. See "Restricted records" above.

verdict.description: `no_matches_found` only when the retrieval was exhaustive; otherwise `inconclusive`. See "The verdict and exhaustiveness" on the endpoint.

query.description: Echo of the request as it was actually applied, including defaulted fields (`limit`, `adjudicate`, `displayThreshold`).

relatedButUnverified.description: Candidates the search layer surfaced but that did not clear the scoring floor. Plain case fields only, no confidence, evidence, partyRole or rationale.

adjudicationsRun.description: How many candidates the LLM actually reviewed on this call, always 0 when `adjudicate` was false.

notice.description: Standing notice about the case removal policy and what a no-match verdict does and does not mean, included on every response.

businessDaysBehind.description: Business days between the latest indexed decision and today. Null when it cannot be computed.

DistrictCourtsRollup.title: DistrictCourtsRollup
DistrictCourtsRollup.description: One rolled up row for every District Court combined: the index carries no state field to break this down further today.

generatedAt.description: When this snapshot was computed, not when this response was served (the snapshot may be served stale from cache).

index.description: The OpenSearch index name this snapshot was computed from.

courts.description: High Courts and tribunals, one row each.
